ompSourceReview.finding: The normal composer requires omp.editor + sendable. Actual installed OMP 18.8.7 owner approval and plan handlers were separately executed through a protocol recorder and through actual Tern.

notes: The production Luau plugin was copied unchanged into the isolated headless fixture.
The synthetic child speaks TSP over Tern's real PTY; no provider credentials were supplied.
Different-user config validation was tested with a mocked current UID because this environment rejects chown.
Tern exposes no canonical OMP conversation or entry IDs; bounded view reconciliation remains conservative.
The strengthened real-owner flow used an unchanged production plugin and bridge, one stock OMP session, the stock mock provider, and an inert extension tool.
The test-only child enables public setTerminalHeadless(false) and PI_TUI_NATIVE=1 so PI_TEST_RUNTIME isolation does not suppress actual TSP negotiation.

Some initial default-worker software-rendered attempts exceeded Tern's 50 ms load/fetch budget. The strengthened final chain passed with Mesa LP_NUM_THREADS=1; this does not establish reliability under every CPU scheduling condition.
TSP activate has no upstream expected-document-revision guard or acknowledged answer transaction; Perch fresh-read validation is not a cross-process compare-and-resolve.
Existing remote-host membership follows the generated SDK and documented window boundary; the daemon test was blocked before attachment, so no remote SSH/tunnel success is claimed.

checks: Exact stock approval picker becomes a complete request and emits the Deny item
An identical replacement component receives a new request identity
Plan document and disabled choices retain owner state; revised plans reject old answers
Oversized and omitted plan content cannot authorize a response
Unrelated modal, filtered selection, and checkbox requests stay on the host
Both stock extension editors remain visible but cannot be answered atomically
Fallback selectors with a strategy slider are read-only
Long approval titles remain complete in the body rather than silently clipped
The selected execution model detail is complete and changes the plan revision
A mounted annotation chooser blocks plan answers and invalidates the visible revision
limitations: Pure mapper in the real Luau VM, using captured stock OMP trees; separate tests cover live Tern reads/event delivery.

checks: A TSP activate reaches the stock tool approval selector and Deny prevents the inert tool from executing.
A new identical approval has a different component ID; an old event cannot approve it, while its own Approve executes the inert tool once.
The actual fallback selector accepts its fully qualified list/item IDs and rejects a disabled option.
A TSP plan choice resolves the stock InteractiveMode plan handler; Refine plan dismisses review, keeps plan mode, and makes no new provider call.
The native plan matches the known source sections; it omits the source title from the body, so the displayed projection is not an exact plan file export.
The stock rich editor advertises sendable:false and ignores atomic send; it must remain unsupported by this first remote request slice.
The stock simple input also advertises sendable:false and ignores atomic send; it remains unsupported.
limitations: Protocol terminal recorder, not a Tern binary or physical phone.
TSP activate has no expected-document revision; fresh host inspection is not an atomic cross-process compare-and-resolve.
Refine plan leaves feedback to the next explicit prompt; section annotation editing is separate.
Both extension rich editors and simple inputs lack atomic native send in this pinned OMP build.

checks: Production plugin and bridge discover an actual OMP process in an actual Tern PTY.
HTTP Deny resolves the native tool approval with no tool execution.
A stale identical request answer is rejected; current Approve executes the inert tool once.
The exact plan heading and all body text are exposed; Refine returns to the real composer.
A separate explicit Unicode feedback prompt enters the original planning conversation.
Approve and keep context continues the original session through the upstream mock provider.
Duplicate receipt lookup and reconnect reads do not repeat effects.
limitations: Headless fixture Tern window, not a restored user desktop or physical Android device.
TSP events have no upstream expected-document-revision guard. Forwarded means event dispatch, not persisted external effects.
actualOwnerCheck.identityAssertions: Nonempty canonical OMP session id is equal on every owner event; every event has the original PID.
actualOwnerCheck.planAssertions: Exact sole top-level title and every body line match the plan file after normalizing only blank-line separation; reopened plan document matches the first projection.

remoteDaemonCheck.reason: The execution environment rejects the Unix socket used by the actual Tern loopback daemon (Operation not permitted).
